content.user_title: Build Real-Time Azure Voice Apps in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Real-time voice applications require complex session, audio, event, and authentication setup. This skill provides focused TypeScript guidance for Azure AI Voice Live integrations.
actual_capabilities: Configure Voice Live clients with Microsoft Entra ID or API key authentication examples.
Set session instructions, voices, models, audio formats, and voice activity detection.
Handle streaming audio, text, transcription, lifecycle, and error events.
Define function tools and return tool results to an active conversation.
Compare supported voice types, models, audio formats, and SDK interfaces.
Show browser microphone access, logging, and subscription cleanup patterns.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not a complete runnable application.
Users need an Azure resource, valid permissions, and compatible audio infrastructure.
The browser example omits the complete audio processing and playback implementation.
The documented SDK version is a beta release, so interfaces may change.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Create a TypeScript prototype that streams microphone audio and receives spoken and text responses.

use_cases.title: Configure Contact Center Audio
use_cases.description: Select telephony audio formats, voice activity detection, and event handlers for live customer conversations.

use_cases.title: Add Voice Tool Calling
use_cases.description: Connect recognized requests to approved application functions and return results into the conversation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal TypeScript setup for Azure AI Voice Live using DefaultAzureCredential. Explain the endpoint, model, session configuration, and cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Node.js voice assistant

prompt_templates.title: Handle Streaming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TypeScript event handlers for streaming audio, text, transcription, connection errors, and session completion. Include safe subscription cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Voice Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a typed weather function to a Voice Live session. Validate arguments, execute the approved function, return its result, and continue the response.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Voice Live architecture for authentication, browser microphone handling, audio formats, reconnection, logging, tool authorization, privacy, and resource cleanup.

output_examples.input: Plan a low-latency Node.js voice assistant with Entra ID and automatic turn detection.
output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with the Azure resource endpoint.
Start a Voice Live session with a real-time model.
Enable audio and text modalities with Azure semantic voice activity detection.
Subscribe to audio, transcript, error, and disconnect events.
Close the subscription when the conversation ends.

output_examples.input: Which audio format should a United States telephony integration use?
output_examples.output: Use G.711 mu-law at 8 kHz when the telephony system expects that format. Confirm codec compatibility before streaming audio.

output_examples.input: Outline safe function calling for a voice weather assistant.
output_examples.output: Allow only the named weather tool, validate its location argument, call the trusted service, return the result, and request the next response.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and keep credentials outside source code.
Validate tool names and arguments before any application function executes.
Handle connection errors and close subscriptions when sessions finish.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys, client secrets, or tenant credentials.
Do not execute arbitrary tool names or unvalidated model-provided arguments.
Do not assume browser audio is ready without permission, conversion, buffering, and playback handling.

faq.question: Which runtimes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Node.js LTS releases and modern browsers using JavaScript or TypeScript.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: Microsoft Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential is recommended. API key authentication is documented as an optional alternative.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused SDK patterns and examples that require integration, testing, and environment-specific code.

faq.question: Can it support telephone audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide lists PCM and G.711 formats, including 8 kHz options commonly used for telephony.

faq.question: Does it explain function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows tool definitions, completed argument events, function results, and response continuation.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before production use?
faq.answer: Review authentication, audio privacy, tool authorization, error recovery, codec compatibility, logging, resource cleanup, and current SDK documentation.
